title: 2018 AMC 10A Problem 21
statement: Which of the following describes the set of values of \(a\) for which the curves \(x^2+y^2=a^2\) and \(y=x^2-a\) in the real \(xy\)-plane intersect at exactly \(3\) points?

solutions.text:
Substitute \(y=x^2-a\) into \(x^2+y^2=a^2\). This gives \(x^2+(x^2-a)^2=a^2\), so \(x^2(x^2-(2a-1))=0\).

The factor \(x^2=0\) always gives the single point \((0,-a)\). The other factor gives two additional real points exactly when \(2a-1>0\).

There are exactly three intersection points when \(a>\dfrac12\). Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Substitute the parabola equation into the circle equation
The nonzero roots appear only when \(2a-1\) is positive
